title: Rapid MRR growth triggers automated PSP account freezes, financially ruining early-stage SaaS startups
description: Early-stage SaaS businesses and digital product creators are being financially ruined by automated risk algorithms from major payment processors (PSPs) like Stripe, Square, and Polar. When a startup experiences 'too fast' Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) growth or a sudden spike in sales, these PSPs flag the account as suspicious and immediately freeze funds, sometimes holding thousands of dollars for months. With no immediate human support to review legitimate business growth, founders face devastating cash flow crises, unable to pay for infrastructure or ads while their revenue is locked in escrow.
the_opportunity: Build a 'startup-friendly' Merchant of Record (MoR) or payment gateway specifically designed for high-growth SaaS and digital products. This solution would replace black-box ML freezing with human-in-the-loop verification for accounts experiencing rapid MRR scaling. Alternatively, create a 'revenue-bridge' factoring service that instantly advances frozen PSP funds to verified businesses while taking over the dispute process with Stripe/Square.
the_gap: There is a massive disconnect between the 'hockey stick growth' that startup culture celebrates and how traditional PSP risk models interpret that same growth (as fraud). Existing processors operate as pseudo-banks but circumvent traditional banking regulations, leaving founders with zero legal recourse when funds are arbitrarily held. Businesses need a payment rail that understands and accommodates rapid, legitimate digital scaling without treating success as a risk indicator.
who_is_affected: High-growth solopreneurs with sudden viral sales
